prompt.context: You are Dean Clark of Harvard Business School. A wealthy benefactor has come to you with the news that she will give HBS $100 million. The grant is contingent upon you using the money effectively. You have 1 week to propose to the benefactor where you would use the money before she will finalize the transfer.
prompt.question: How would you, as Dean Clark, propose to use this $100 million?

framework: Treat HBS as a business: identify all major revenue streams and assess relative profitability
Map the four major business units: MBA program, Executive Education, Publishing, Grants and Donations
Analyze what drives each revenue stream to identify the root business driver
Determine where $100M investment produces the greatest return across all units
Synthesize into a final recommendation with supporting rationale

questions.prompt: What are the major revenue streams (business units) of HBS?
questions.guidance: A strong answer identifies the four main revenue streams: MBA program, Executive Education, Publishing, and Grants and Donations. Candidate should note that while other initiatives (e.g., distance learning) exist, these four are the largest sources of revenue.

questions.prompt: How do the four business units compare in terms of relative profitability?
questions.guidance: Executive Education is very profitable because fees charged are large relative to program length. Publishing is highly profitable. Grants and donations are virtually pure profit. The MBA program is likely the least profitable of the four on a direct basis.

questions.prompt: Given that the MBA program appears least profitable, should Dean Clark deprioritize it in favor of higher-margin units?
questions.guidance: No. A strong candidate recognizes that the HBS brand drives the value of all other revenue streams. Executive Education attendance and price premium are driven by the HBS brand. Publishing credibility and sales rely on the HBS brand. Grants and donations flow largely from alumni of the MBA program. The MBA program is the root driver of the brand and therefore of all other revenue streams.

questions.prompt: Where should the $100 million be invested?
questions.guidance: The $100M should be invested in the MBA program. Maintaining the MBA program's reputation as the premier program attracts the best professors and students. Professors publish, supporting the Publishing revenue stream. MBA graduates achieve notable success, further strengthening the brand. Alumni are the primary source of grants and donations. Thus, investing in the MBA program produces returns across all four revenue streams, both directly and via brand enhancement.

recommendation: Invest the $100 million in the MBA program, as it is the foundational driver of the HBS brand and all other revenue streams
By strengthening the MBA program, HBS enhances the brand that supports Executive Education pricing power, Publishing credibility, and alumni-driven Grants and Donations
risks: Over-investing in the MBA program at the expense of innovation in newer channels such as distance learning
Brand dependency on a single program creates concentration risk if MBA market dynamics shift
next_steps: Define specific MBA program enhancements (faculty, facilities, scholarships, curriculum) that maximize brand and educational quality
Monitor ROI on investment across all four business units to validate brand amplification effects
